decisions.reason: F3 cited a linear-only measure theorem for the affine contraction. Added the published translation-invariance supplier and derived affine integral scaling by indicators, simple approximation, and signed parts. The s^(-d/2) pullback bound, weak derivative factor s, inward collar, and L2 mollification convergence now follow with unchanged Statement. This is a local citation/derivation omission, not a counterexample to density.

The original Definition invoked the quotient and bounded weak normal trace of lem-na-hdiv-weak-normal-trace without its explicit Countable Choice hypothesis. That supplier, and the underlying H1 and H1_0 interfaces, require it. Added precisely this hypothesis and its dependency; the kernel-of-Green-functional definition and arbitrary-open-domain scope are unchanged. All ten direct item consumers explicitly assume Countable Choice.

The mesh-space definition only supplies RT/BDM notation for d=2,3, whereas the algebraic Piola argument is valid in every positive dimension. Preserved the full claim by explicitly defining the real polynomial families in the Statement for every d>=1, and qualified F2 as agreement with the existing d=2,3 convention. Polynomial degree decomposition and the inverse map prove bijectivity; k=0 has zero remainder. No new theorem or weakened conclusion is needed.

A1 correctly identifies inherited Countable Choice: the original weak-normal-trace lemma explicitly assumes it, as do the H1 and H1_0 interfaces, and the kernel lemma explicitly assumes it in its own Statement. The omitted restatement in the original H0(div) definition did not make those suppliers choice-free. For v_h in V_h its divergence is cellwise constant with zero mean, so testing by that divergence proves both kernel inclusions, including Q_h={0}. No item edit is warranted.

The Statement explicitly takes S_h:Q_h->V_h to be the stable right inverse above, rather than claiming such a lift for arbitrary domains. These are the V_h,Q_h of the cited mesh convention (d=2,3; bounded connected polyhedral Lipschitz D), and the referenced lift theorem supplies precisely its uniform C_R. Independently, given that lift, Pi_h v=S_h P0 div v+P_Z(v-S_h P0 div v) is a projection on any such pair: P_Z is an L2 contraction, its divergence is zero, and reproduction and the bound 1+sqrt(1+C_R^2)+C_R follow. Thus the rejection discards the explicit stable-lift premise and existing mesh notation; no claim or proof repair is needed.

The cited Galerkin theorem names exact bilinear-form norms, while F4 proves only upper bounds. Replaced the erroneous equality inference by m_a=||a||<=M_a and m_b=||b||<=M_b, applied the supplier with m_a,m_b, and then proved successive monotonicity of R_h,U_h,P_h under replacing beta_h^(-1),m_a,m_b by their larger displayed bounds. The lift also explicitly supplies nonzero V_h when Q_h is nonzero. The Statement, weighted flux bound, one-cell branch, and permeability-contrast caveat remain intact.
